name: Hiver
tagline: Customer support and shared inbox workflows inside Gmail

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited users; 1 shared inbox; 1 tag; 1 email template; 1 send-from alias; 6 months of analytics history.
tiers.notes: Hiver in Gmail free plan; a Gmail or Google Workspace account is still required.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: Up to 10 users; 2 shared inboxes; 10 automations per shared inbox; 2 custom fields; 12 months analytics history.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited users; 5 shared inboxes; 20 automations per shared inbox; 10 custom fields; 18 months analytics history.

tiers.name: Elite
tiers.limits: Unlimited users, shared inboxes, automations and custom fields; 6 custom roles; 24 months analytics history.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free forever: unlimited users, 1 shared inbox, 1 tag, 1 email template, 1 send-from alias and 6 months of analytics history
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; 7-day Elite trial with no credit card, then choose Free or a paid plan
pricing.hiddenCosts: Paid plans start at 2 seats; seat counts can move from 2 to 5 and then only in increments of 5. Hiver in Gmail also requires a separate Gmail or Google Workspace account; Growth is capped at 10 users.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Hiver's durable value is deliverability, security, integration, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local email companion for Gmail shared inbox that works on exported mail or one user-authorized IMAP account.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: IMAP or Gmail OAuth credentials where supported
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: team routing and shared inbox rules
whyPeopleStillPay: Hiver: Email is infrastructure. Customers pay to avoid lost messages, broken auth, spam problems, and the reputational cost of a flaky inbox.
ongoingBurden: Own OAuth refresh, IMAP quirks, encryption, spam handling, notification delivery, and provider policy changes.

priorArt.name: Mailspring
priorArt.desc: Open-source desktop mail client and useful IMAP prior art.

alternatives.name: Chatwoot
alternatives.desc: A proper support inbox with assignments and automations; it replaces the Gmail skin rather than living inside it.

facts.install: Docker Compose on a Linux VM, followed by environment, database, reverse-proxy and TLS configuration
facts.dataFormat: Application data in PostgreSQL, queues/cache in Redis, and attachments on local disk or S3-compatible/cloud object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Assignments and private notes work, but the team leaves Gmail and does support in a separate application.
facts.setupBlocker: Provisioning a Linux server and correctly wiring DNS/TLS, SMTP, PostgreSQL/Redis and storage

alternatives.name: Frappe Helpdesk
alternatives.desc: Clean shared support queues, assignments and SLAs; installing Frappe is the first ticket.

facts.install: Run Frappe's easy-install script against the stable container image on a Linux server
facts.dataFormat: Tickets in the Frappe site database, with public and private attachments in the site's files directories
facts.gapVsPaid: It replaces Hiver's native Gmail workflow with a separate ticket queue and a Frappe server to operate.
facts.setupBlocker: A Linux server, domain/DNS, Docker or the easy-install script, and mail account configuration

alternatives.name: FreeScout
alternatives.desc: Shared mailboxes, assignments and internal notes without per-agent rent; you leave Gmail for PHP and MySQL.

facts.install: Install on a PHP/MySQL host with its web installer, or deploy a community Docker image
facts.dataFormat: Mailboxes, users and conversation metadata in the configured SQL database, with attachments in application server storage
facts.gapVsPaid: You leave Gmail for a PHP/MySQL web app, and several advanced channels and features are separate paid modules.
facts.setupBlocker: A web server/database plus IMAP/SMTP credentials; several advanced channels and features require separate modules

alternatives.name: Zammad
alternatives.desc: Mature ticketing, ownership and team workflows; Gmail becomes an input channel, not the workplace.

facts.install: Deploy the Docker Compose/Portainer stack or install supported Linux packages
facts.dataFormat: Ticket and user data in PostgreSQL, search indexes in Elasticsearch, and attachments/backups in Docker volumes or server storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Gmail becomes an input channel rather than the workplace, with heavier ticket semantics and server operations.
facts.setupBlocker: A comparatively large server and familiarity with Docker/Portainer, PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch

notes: Credibility row: Hiver survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Hiver; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local email companion for Gmail shared inbox that works on exported mail or one user-authorized IMAP account.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: team routing and shared inbox rules; abuse response and security operations; provider-grade deliverability.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
